item.title: Understanding the Implications of the U.S.-Venezuela Oil Deal
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Senior Associate Jose Ignacio Hernández explains the U.S.-Venezuela oil agreement and examines its implications for U.S. energy policy and Venezuela’s political transition.

item.title: Nicaragua’s Dictatorship Deepens: What Can the International Community Do?
item.description: CSIS Americas Program experts evaluate next steps for the United States and the international community amid further authoritarian consolidation by the Ortega-Murillo regime in Nicaragua.

item.title: U.S.-Africa Trade at a Crossroads: A Moment for New Thinking
item.description: AGOA has been extended for two years, but U.S.-Africa trade remains stagnant. The extension provides an opportunity to develop a new framework that meets the commercial goals and ambitions of the United States and African countries.

item.title: The End of American Sanctuary
item.description: In Foreign Affairs, Seth Jones argues new threats demand new U.S. homeland defense strategies

item.title: Own Goals
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch examines a series of "own goals" caused not by a mistake during a crisis but by a failure of good governance.

item.title: The Pacific Is Ground Zero for Deep-Sea Mining
item.description: The race for critical minerals race is moving offshore, and the Pacific is ground zero.

item.title: (Still) Awaiting Launch: Space Export Control Reform
item.description: U.S. space companies deserve a level playing field abroad. Long-awaited export control reforms must account for foreign competition, strengthen international partnerships, and keep pace with a rapidly changing global market.

item.title: Strategic Partnerships to Secure Critical Resources and Supply Chains
item.description: The United States does not have sufficient domestic geological resources to meet its mineral needs for sectors vital to national security, economic competitiveness, and energy resilience. International partnerships not optional; they are a fundamental component of U.S. mineral security.
